newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end tad higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end tad higher.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended a tad higher across the board in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Tuesday.
"Bond prices rose a tad higher but treasury bills eased slightly again today. The interbank rate remained unchanged as yesterday's. Volume was only moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.88/1.83 percent compared with Monday's yield of 1.90/1.85 percent and one-year remained unchanged at a yield of 2.20/2.15 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.07/98.12 from Monday's close of S$98.00/98.05, September 2001 at S$97.05/99.15 versus S$97.00/97.05 and June 2003 at S$95.05/95.10 against S$95.00/95.05.
The overnight interbank offered rate remained at 2-5/8 2-1/4 percent.
